findings.evidence: Lines 112–123 prove `(toCartierDivisor X).comp ((toRationalUnitSheaf X).hom.app ...).hom = 0`, while lines 127–141 separately transport through `rationalUnitSectionsEquiv`; `RationalFunctions.lean:334–339` confirms the required compatibility with `X.germToFunctionField`, but this PR supplies no public high-level quotient lemma.
findings.fix: Expose the canonical map from units of `Γ(X, ⊤)` to `X.functionFieldˣ` (or state the result directly using `Units.map (X.germToFunctionField ⊤)`) and add an appropriately `[simp]`-annotated theorem that its principal Cartier divisor is zero.
findings.issue: `principalCartierDivisor` has no theorem saying that a global regular unit, mapped into `X.functionFieldˣ`, has zero divisor; the existing line 112 lemma only characterizes the lower-level sheaf-section map and leaves consumers to unfold and reconcile `rationalUnitSectionsEquiv`.

summary: The sheaf-level quotient API is adequate, but the principal-divisor interface omits its essential regular-unit quotient law.
